guidelines.detail: documentation rule PROC-05 not applied (The description places optional feedback after resolution, while the validator reports a detached start-to-end chain. PROC-05 already covers triggers after the main flow and allows a gateway connection, an event subprocess, or a separate process.)

refines FID-01 (The description places optional feedback after the case is resolved. The generated model instead uses a feedback start and end event, while the reference models feedback as an activity. This refines FID-01 by specifying how to model an optional activity that follows the main process outcome. The wording check flagged “resolved” as process-specific, so the trigger uses the more general “main proces)

same as LRN-027 (The validator records a detached start-to-end flow, while the description places optional feedback after the case is resolved. This supports modeling the activity as a continuation, and learned guideline LRN-027 already states essentially the same rule.)

same as LRN-027 (The description places optional feedback after resolution, while the generated model represents it with separate start and end events and lacks the corresponding activity. This is already captured by LRN-027; the documented guidelines do not contradict it.)

same as LRN-027 (The description places optional feedback after case resolution, while the generated model represents it with a separate start and end event and the reference models it as an activity. This is already captured by learned guideline LRN-027.)

same as LRN-027 (The description places optional feedback after resolution (S5–S6), while the structural records indicate a feedback decision and feedback event in the reference structure (M2–M3). This supports modeling the optional response after the outcome; the same principle is already captured by learned guideline LRN-027.)

same as LRN-020 (The description says customers provide feedback, while the generated label says they receive it, changing the action’s direction. This supports preserving the described action and direction in task labels, which is already covered by learned guideline LRN-020.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says optional behavior may occur after the main flow has completed

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a participant may perform an optional activity after the main process outcome has been reached: Model that activity as an optional continuation of the same process, rather than as a new process initiated by the activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant may perform an optional activity after the main process outcome has been reached

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description distinguishes an event or activity by its action, actor, object, recipient, or another meaningful qualifier: Label each BPMN element so that it preserves those stated details without substituting a broader or different meaning.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity and identifies its action, object, actor, or recipient.
